Reviewer pass 1 and pass 2 on `units.json` (56 units). `t` was not touched (asserted by script: every `t`, `ln`, `p`, `mark`, `v` and the title fields are identical before and after). `gloss.json` was not read or touched; it is for the later reviewer pass.

Checked and found sound: every `t` joins back to the packet's 95 lines exactly; `ln` values; `p` on 719, 733, 764, 767, 778, 792 (the six ¶ of the packet); `mark` on the first unit of each speech (757 Hera, 765 Zeus, 787 Stentor/Hera, 800 Athena); quotation marks (“ on 757, 765, 787, 800; ” on 762, 766, 791, 813; the neighbouring part's last unit, 5.718, ends with ”, so unit 0 correctly opens without one); `l` has the same number of lines as `t`; no `\n` in `i`; typographic ’ only; cross-references 2.166, 1.499, 1.560, 4.59, 4.384–390, 5.262, 5.521, 3.263, 3.362 and Odyssey 11.634 and 1.100–101 each found in the published files and each true of what the note says; whole-line repeats (5.719, 5.764) match the published English; 5.754 matches 1.499; 5.746–747 matches Odyssey 1.100–101.

### Hand scan of the flagged line 745
ἐς δ’ ὄχεα φλόγεα ποσὶ βήσετο, λάζετο δ’ ἔγχος has 17 syllables, so it must be six feet with the first five dactyls: ἐς ὄ-χε | α φλό-γε | α πο-σὶ | βή-σε-το | λά-ζε-το | δ’ ἔγ-χος. Foot 1: ἐς is long by position before δ’. Foot 2: the short α of ὄχεα before φλ- may count long (mute and liquid). Foot 3: the α of φλόγεα, short by nature and followed by a single consonant (π), is in the long place; it is long only by licence (the scanner's "metrical lengthening … longum of foot 3", at the main break). Synizesis of ὄχεα or φλόγεα does not rescue it (tried: it leaves the first foot or the second without its two shorts). So the irregularity is real and one note sentence was added at 745 (unit 15).

## Considered and refused

- **Unit 10 (736), θωρήσσετο an imperfect, `l`/`i` "armed herself"**: a simple past is a normal English rendering of an imperfect after a completed participle ("having put on … armed herself"); the table's "were arming themselves" (4.252) is for a plural scene. Kept.
- **Unit 4 (726), περίδρομοι "running round"** against the table's "that can be run round" (2.812): that row is the other sense of the word, of a hill with room to run round it; here it describes how silver is set on a hub, and the note says the sense is not clear. Kept.
- **Unit 5 (727), δίφρος "chariot-board"** against the table's δίφρος "chariot": the word is plainly the floor of the car here (the note says so), and "chariot-board" keeps the table word. Kept.
- **Unit 9 (733), ἑανός "fine"**: consistent with 3.385 policy of hedging in the note; note already says the sense is uncertain. Kept.
- **Unit 17 (749) and 18 (750) the `i` of unit 20 (753) beginning "They found" after a `;`**: `i` sentences may begin afresh where `l` continues ("and they found"); only capitalisations that contradict the previous `i`'s own punctuation (748, 784) were changed.
- **Unit 28 (768), `i` "and the pair flew, not unwilling," against the published "the pair flew not unwilling"**: the comma is needed because the sentence goes on ("between earth and starry heaven"); the unit is not identical to the published one. Kept.
- **Unit 36 (784), `i` "who could shout as loud as fifty other men" (a finite "could" for a form the note says it cannot fully parse)**: the sense is not in doubt and the note says so; any other English would be a longer guess. Kept.
- **Unit 38 (788), `l` "never did the Trojans … use to go about"**: odd English but the literal gloss of οὐδέ ποτε … οἴχνεσκον; `i` carries the plain version. Kept.
- **Unit 43 (794), `l` "which Pandarus hit him with, with an arrow"**: clumsy, but it keeps βάλε and ἰῷ distinct in Greek order. Kept.
- **Unit 54 (811), `i` "a weariness that darts upon you again and again"**: "again and again" comes from πολυ- "much"; the note says the exact force is not known. Kept.
- **Unit 22 (757), the cut at "οὐ κατὰ κόσμον" where the edition prints no stop**: segmentation is outside this brief; the syntax breaks there (the period runs five lines, 757–761), and the drafter's cut is defensible under the four-line rule. Kept.
- **Unit 7 (729), "the unnamed subject … is still Hebe"**: a reading, not a label; the Greek leaves the subject open until Ἥρη at 731, and the note says "unnamed". Kept.
- **Unit 15 (745), "ἐς … βήσετο … an epic mixed aorist"**: βήσετο is the sigmatic aorist with the thematic vowel, which is what "mixed" names. Kept.
- **Unit 28 (768), τὼ as "the two horses" rather than the two goddesses**: either is defensible; the note says "(the two horses)" and the same line is used of horses at 5.366. Kept.
- **Unit 35 (780), l/i "most … best"**: "the most and the best" (l) and "the greatest number and the best" (i) agree in force. Kept.

### Considered and left

- αὐδήσασχ’: parsed as aorist iterative of αὐδάω; the unit note says it "looks like" the aorist participle. Both are defensible; the entry's parse suits the sense ("used to shout") and was left.
- ἐξαποδίωμαι: lemma ἐξαποδίεμαι is constructed and the entry hedges ("archaic"); the subjunctive parse fits the line, so left.
- τελαμῶνος (Telamon) and οἷσίν (possessive ὅς): second readings are genuine homographs, kept under the " · " rule though only one reading is used here.
- ἐδείδισαν, κεντρηνεκέας, ὑψηχέες, ἀγελείην: etymologies/senses already hedged in the entries; left.
- All 28 `__broaden__` additions: each reading is attested in this part (checked against the Greek) and none duplicates the old entry; no refusals of the glosser's work there. No change.
